$comment: Gears & Bells in the Clock Court (docs/specs/ISLAND-07-tidewheel-caldera.md §5): the clock desk (Edit), the day gear (Manual to Daily), the ring’s crank (Hours: 08:00; the dial), the peg board (clear the other hours; Minute :00), the save bell (Save automation; the card and Automation details), the tide gauge (a local run needs the computer awake) and the morning log (Recent runs; tighten a noisy prompt). The places, lamps and the Lighthouse’s clock ring are the game’s; every word is this file’s.

tide.name: The tide gauge
tide.means: The computer awake, and the app running

text.title: Gears & Bells
text.intro: Open the automation, seat the day gear, set the ring, clear the pegs, save it, read the tide, and check the morning log.

laps.title: Gears & Bells: schedule the report
laps.order: PR review readiness report · Daily at 08:00

stations.title: Open the automation
stations.prompt: The manual report worked. How do you start to put it on the clock?

options.text: Open **Automations**, select your `PR review readiness report`, then select **Edit**
options.result: The ledger opens at the report’s page.

options.text: Select **New automation**, and build a second report
options.reason: Schedule the automation you tested. Select it, then select **Edit**.
A scheduled run appears without you selecting **Run**.

stations.title: Seat the day gear
stations.prompt: The **Trigger** shows **Manual**. What do you change it to, so the summary is waiting each morning?

options.result: The day gear meshes with the clock train.

options.text: **Hourly**, to be sure it is fresh
options.reason: The course schedules it daily, before the workday starts. If a scheduled run is noisy, you run the schedule less often, not more.
Then it still runs only when you start it. Change the **Trigger** from **Manual** to **Daily**.

stations.title: Set the ring
stations.prompt: Turn the crank, and watch the ring on the Lighthouse’s clock. Which hour does the report run at?

positions.result: The marker stands on eight: a time before the workday starts.

positions.reason: That’s the default hour, and the day watch has started by then. Select a time before your workday starts.
The workday has started. The summary should be waiting when you start your day.
The workday has started. Select a time before your workday starts.
Half the day is gone. Select a time before your workday starts, for example **08:00**.

hints: When does the day watch start?

stations.title: Clear the pegs
stations.prompt: **08:00** is selected in **Hours**. The default **09:00** is selected too. What do you do?

options.text: Clear **09:00**, so that only **08:00** remains selected, and keep **Minute** at **:00**
options.result: The nine peg comes out. One peg in the ring.

options.text: Leave both: the first one wins
options.reason: This field allows more than one hour. Clear any other selected hours, so that only your chosen hour remains selected.

options.text: Set **Minute** to **:30** to split the difference
options.reason: Keep **Minute** at **:00**. Clear the other hour.

stations.title: Save it, and check
stations.caption: **Automation details**, after the schedule is saved.
stations.prompt: You select **Save automation**. How do you confirm the schedule?

options.text: The card shows the **Daily** trigger. Open the automation and select its name: **Automation details** shows the **Schedule** and the **Next run** time
options.result: The striking figures ring once. Daily at 8:00 AM, and a next run.

options.text: No need to check: saving is enough
options.reason: After saving, check the automation card and **Automation details**.

options.text: Select **Run automation** to see if the schedule works
options.reason: That starts a manual run now. The schedule is shown in **Automation details**, with the **Next run** time.

hints: The card shows **Daily**. **Automation details** shows the **Schedule** and **Next run**.

stations.title: Read the tide
stations.prompt: This automation is local. What must be true at 08:00 tomorrow for the run to happen?

options.text: My computer is awake, and the GitHub Copilot app is running
options.result: The float rises. Tide in, and the wheel turns.

options.text: Nothing: a schedule runs whatever my computer is doing
options.reason: If your computer is asleep at the scheduled time, the run does not happen.

options.text: Nothing: a missed run starts when I open the app later
options.reason: A scheduled local run happens only when your computer is awake and the GitHub Copilot app is running.

hints: The computer awake, and the app running.

stations.title: The next morning
stations.text: The next morning, check **Recent runs** and confirm a new run completed. If the app was running at the scheduled time, the new run appears under **Recent runs** without you selecting **Run**.

stations.title: Keep it useful
stations.prompt: After a few runs, the summary is too long and noisy. What do you do?

options.text: Tighten the prompt: for example, limit it to pull requests with failing checks, then save again
options.result: A shorter page in the log, and every line worth reading.

options.reason: A human reviews the result. If the result is noisy, you know where to narrow the prompt.

options.text: Run it more often, so each run is shorter
options.reason: Narrow the prompt, run the schedule less often, or add a label or branch filter to reduce the output.

hints: Limit it, for example to pull requests with failing checks, then save again.
